guarantees.claim: phase1_in is always driven with the value of state_in
phase2_in is always driven with the value of phase1_out
state_out is always driven with the value of phase2_out

assumptions.claim: state_in must be held stable and valid during the entire time phase1 consumes phase1_in
assumptions.cond: when the Keccak phase1 stage is active
assumptions.risk: changing state_in mid‑computation corrupts phase1_out and eventually state_out, undermining Keccak output integrity

assumptions.claim: phase1_out must be a complete and stable result from the phase1 processing stage before phase2 samples phase2_in
assumptions.cond: when phase2 uses phase2_in (sampling edge or enable)
assumptions.risk: premature or unstable phase1_out leads to incorrect input to phase2, producing a wrong state_out

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational path from state_in → phase1_in → phase1_out → phase2_in → phase2_out → state_out can propagate a new state_in value all the way to state_out during an ongoing computation if state_in changes while phase1 or phase2 is still processing previous data.
uncertain_points.cond: when state_in updates while phase1/phase2 are enabled or have unfinished work
uncertain_points.risk: state_out may capture a mixture of old and new data, causing Keccak output corruption or non‑deterministic behavior

uncertain_points.claim: The unconditional combinational connection from phase1_out to phase2_in assumes that the phase2 block will only sample phase2_in when phase1_out is valid and stable, but no handshake or enable signal is visible in this chunk.
uncertain_points.cond: if phase2 lacks a valid/ready handshake or the handshake is misaligned
uncertain_points.risk: phase2 could latch intermediate or stale data, producing an incorrect state_out and possibly violating Keccak functional correctness
